issues.description: The problem specification and solution expect a function named make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None, but the template repository defines create_y_state(...) instead. This name mismatch is structural: students following the template will not find the expected make_y_state symbol to implement or tests expecting make_y_state will fail. The template even references make_y_state in its NotImplementedError text, adding to the confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function create_y_state to make_y_state and ensure its signature matches make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None. Also update any internal references and the NotImplementedError message to consistently use make_y_state so students implement the function the tests expect.

issues.description: The problem statement and tests refer to a function named make_y_state(...) to prepare a noisy |Y> ancilla, but the template implementation defines create_y_state(...) instead (and its NotImplementedError message even references make_y_state). The solution implements make_y_state(...). This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual entity (preparing a noisy |Y> resource state) will confuse students and break automated tests that expect make_y_state.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function create_y_state(...) to make_y_state(...) and update its internal error message and any references to use make_y_state so the template, problem statement, and solution use the same identifier for the |Y> state preparation function.
